_comment: Every figure in this file is quoted from a Sheffield City Council Infrastructure Funding Statement, which the council must publish each year under the CIL (Amendment) (England) (No.2) Regulations 2019. Sheffield publishes nothing to the national planning-development-data dataset, so these statements are the only published account of what the council has received and what it is holding.

_definitions.s106_receipts_in_year: paragraph 4.10: money actually received in the year
_definitions.s106_balance_retained: the council's own 'Current S106 Balance' paragraph
_definitions.s106_agreements_signed: paragraph 4.8. Not one measure across the six years: up to 2022/23 the wording is 'N S106 agreements were signed', from 2023/24 it is 'N S106 agreements (including deed of variations and supplemental deeds)'. The counts either side of that change are not comparable.
_definitions.cil_unallocated: Table 1: CIL received up to and including the reported year, less the amount allocated to projects
_definitions.unspent_at_year_end: derived: S106 balance retained plus unallocated CIL

corroborating.claim: S106 received £1.2m, spent £4.1m, held £15.3m; CIL received £2.6m, spent £1.6m, held £9.2m, all for 2024/25
corroborating.verification: read directly from the page by this repository
corroborating.what_it_actually_is: Not independent. The page attributes every figure to 'Sheffield's latest Infrastructure Funding Statement (2024/25)', and each one matches the IFS to the rounding. It is a republication. Its one useful signal: an independent extraction of the same PDF also read the misprinted balance as £15.3m rather than £153m.

corroborating.claim: Sheffield has collected £33m of CIL in total since charging began on 15 July 2015 (rank 51); nationally 47% of all CIL ever raised was unspent by 2025 (£2.2bn), against 42% up to 2023-24, implying a spend lag of just under four years
corroborating.verification: read directly from the report PDF by this repository
corroborating.why_it_matters: Sheffield's unallocated CIL of £9.2m is about 28% of its £33m lifetime collections, below the 47% national figure, so on CIL at least Sheffield spends faster than the average authority. The report also warns its unspent figures come from HBF FOI data of 'doubtful value', so this is a rough benchmark, not a verdict.

cannot_corroborate.finding: Sheffield's audited accounts do not disclose Section 106 or CIL as a separate line, so they can neither confirm nor contradict the IFS balances
cannot_corroborate.verification: full-text searched by this repository: 190 pages, zero occurrences of 'Section 106' or 'S106'; 'Community Infrastructure Levy' appears only in two service-variance explanations (£170k, £14k) and the standard accounting-policy note
cannot_corroborate.where_it_is_buried: Developer contributions sit inside 'Capital grants and contributions credited to the CI&ES' (Note 8), which for 2024/25 is £94,923k, and in the Capital Grants Unapplied Reserve, which also holds every other unapplied capital grant. Both are aggregates over all grants, so neither is a developer-contribution figure.

cannot_corroborate.finding: The South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority, the body Sheffield sits inside, publishes no developer-contribution figures at all
cannot_corroborate.verification: reported by a research pass over SYMCA's audited accounts 2022/23 to 2024/25, auditor's annual reports and capital investment programme reports; not independently re-run by this repository
cannot_corroborate.why: Combined authorities are not charging or collecting authorities for CIL, and are not a local planning authority, so they neither sign S106 deeds nor levy CIL. Sheffield's developer-contribution position is entirely a Sheffield City Council position.

unresolved.finding: Sheffield told an FOI requester on 31 October 2024 that it held no S106 contributions past their clawback date, then on 30 September 2026 disclosed a spreadsheet of unspent S106 contributions that had passed their expiry dates
unresolved.verification: NOT VERIFIED. WhatDoTheyKnow is behind Cloudflare and returns 403 to this repository. The attachments (EIR 3286690.xlsx, Book2.xlsx, EIR 2695294.xlsx) could not be downloaded.
unresolved.why_it_matters: If the 2026 spreadsheet is not empty then money sat past the point at which it had to be offered back, which is the single strongest finding available on Sheffield's S106 practice. It needs a browser to read, so it is flagged here rather than asserted.

unresolved.finding: A written answer at Full Council on 8 September 2021 put unspent S106 at £19.4m, of which £14.7m was committed, across 234 wholly or partially unspent agreements
unresolved.verification: NOT VERIFIED. democracy.sheffield.gov.uk returns 403 to this repository. Reported by a research pass; consistent with the IFS balance of £18,958,520 at 31 March 2021, which is why it is worth chasing.
